text:
Alex: quick question — toggled an internal feature-flag that flips off a non-public optimization. does this deserve a patch tag (v1.2.4) or can we just promote on main with no tag? trying to keep release noise low.

DeployBot: deploy queued: main -> production at 11:30 PT. No tag provided. Use `git tag` or `/deploy tag v1.2.4` to attach a release tag. :warning:

Maria: i vote for tagging. even small toggles are config changes that affect runtime behavior. traceability wins.

Jon: we used to skip tags for purely telemetry-only changes, but that made rollbacks a mess. i'd prefer a lightweight rule: if it changes behavior or surface (even behind a flag) => patch bump.

Tanvi: proposal: semantic rule =
- patch: backward-compatible bug fixes, config/flag changes that alter behavior
- minor: new feature behind flag or new public API
- major: breaking changes

This keeps it conservative and consistent. :thinking:

Liam: +1 to the conservative approach. also: tag format should always be `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (annotated tag) and release notes created via our release-bot. e.g.

```
# tag locally
git tag -a v1.2.4 -m "patch: fix timeout flag"
git push origin v1.2.4

# or via bot
/deploy tag v1.2.4
```

Maria: also add a tiny PR checklist snippet that the bot can surface:
- PR body must include `changelog: patch: short description`
- if omitted, release-bot will prompt one reviewer to add it before tagging

Example PR body line:
```
changelog: patch: disable speculative optimization behind flag due to latency spike
```

Jon: rollback playbook note: prefer redeploying a previous tag instead of reverting commits on main. keeps history clean. command we use is `./deploy --tag v1.2.3 --env prod` or `/deploy rollback v1.2.3` in the channel.

DeployBot: rollback supported. Use `/deploy rollback v1.2.3` — will run canary -> full and alert on SLO regressions. :white_check_mark:

Alex: sounds good. what about branch naming for urgent fixes? hotfix/ vs release/ ?

Tanvi: use `hotfix/<version>` for ad-hoc urgent fixes that bypass main QA queues. otherwise create `release/<version>` for planned rollouts.

Liam: and add an automated check that annotated tags include the `changelog:` entry in the release body. that keeps release notes machine-readable for cost/latency dashboards.

Maria: TL;DR decision: tag everything that changes runtime behavior with `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (annotated), require `changelog: patch:` line in PR body, use `hotfix/*` branches for urgent rollouts, and rollback by redeploying previous tag. i'll update the release playbook and PR template.

Alex: excellent — Maria can you drop a short blurb in #eng-docs and update the PR template? :thumbsup:

Maria: will do, put the checklist in the release docs and i'll wire the bot prompts tomorrow.

Jon: thanks all. :shipit:
